subtitle: Rank, compare, and aggregate without collapsing: OVER clauses, tie-correct rankings, neighbor navigation, frame mastery, and staged window programs
audience: Developers comfortable with GROUP BY, subqueries, and CTEs (SQL Intermediate; the ranking primer in SQL Advanced Ch.5 is helpful but repeated briefly here) who need leaderboards, top-N-per-group, running totals, deltas, and quantile tiers. Flat baseline queries run in the SQL Query Sandbox; all window SQL targets real SQLite or PostgreSQL with engine differences called out explicitly.
outcomes: Decompose any OVER clause into partition, ordering, and frame — and predict peer sets exactly
Exploit evaluation order: windows over grouped output, rank-inside/filter-outside staging
Choose ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, and NTILE by contract, with deterministic tiebreakers
Navigate with LAG/LEAD/FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE, including framing fixes and named WINDOWs
Command ROWS, RANGE, and GROUPS frames plus EXCLUDE for moving, peer, and tier logic
Compose FILTER metrics, QUALIFY emulations, and multi-stage window programs through CTEs
Deliver tiered, cliff-measured, context-rich analyses as cited findings with caveats

assessment.q: SUM(x) OVER (PARTITION BY role) vs SUM(x) OVER (PARTITION BY role ORDER BY x) — difference?
options: Whole-partition total vs growing-prefix running total — ORDER BY flips the default frame
assessment.explain: OVER's ORDER BY sequences peers and switches defaults to running. Same function, different peer sets (Ch.1).

assessment.q: Why must WHERE rn <= 2 wrap the ROW_NUMBER query instead of sharing its level?
options: Pipeline order: WHERE evaluates before windows exist — compute inside, filter outside
assessment.explain: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → windows → SELECT → ORDER BY. Same-level filtering predates the alias (Ch.1).

assessment.q: Fixed 10-row feed uses RANK and shows 9–12 rows intermittently. Fix and reason?
options: ROW_NUMBER with deterministic order — exactly 10 numbers always exist; RANK shares on ties
assessment.explain: Cardinality contracts: ROW_NUMBER guarantees N rows; RANK guarantees honest ties. Slot type dictates function (Ch.2).

assessment.q: 14 rows into NTILE(4). Sizes and rule?
options: 4,4,3,3 — differ by ≤1, earlier buckets take remainders
assessment.explain: 14 = 3×4 + 2: first two buckets absorb remainders. Persist labels; boundaries drift with growth (Ch.2).

assessment.q: LAST_VALUE(x) OVER (PARTITION BY r ORDER BY h DESC) returns each row's own value. Why + fix?
options: Default growing frame makes it 'last so far' — add ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
assessment.explain: ORDER BY flips defaults to running prefix; LAST_VALUE then reads the current row. Full frame is the mandatory pairing (Ch.3).

assessment.q: LAG(x, 1) on the first ordered row yields?
options: NULL (no previous row) unless a default is supplied
assessment.explain: Edges lack neighbors. Self-defaults (LAG(x,1,x)) keep edge arithmetic clean (Ch.3).

assessment.q: ROWS vs RANGE frames on tied ORDER BY values?
options: ROWS splits ties across windows by position; RANGE carries each tie group together by value
assessment.explain: Positions vs values is the frame decision; ties expose it. Choose by whether ties must travel together (Ch.4).

assessment.q: 'Average of everyone else in my group' needs?
options: Full-partition frame with EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW — removes self-bias
assessment.explain: Baselines must exclude the subject. EXCLUDE sculpts exactly that (Ch.4).

assessment.q: Translate Snowflake QUALIFY rnk <= 3 to SQLite/PostgreSQL.
options: Subquery/CTE wrapper: compute window inside, filter alias outside
assessment.explain: No QUALIFY here: pipeline order forces the wrapper. Mechanical translation, identical rows (Ch.5).

assessment.q: NTILE tier labels from January vs March disagree on the same learners. Proper handling?
options: Persist labels with as-of dates; recomputed quantiles drift — undated tiers are incomparable
assessment.explain: Quantile boundaries move with data. Comparability requires versioned labels (Ch.6).

project.title: Leaderboard, Tiers & Cliffs
project.summary: Build the engagement leaderboard suite for the DevPath catalog: deterministic global ranking, per-role top-3, quartile tiers with cliffs, and role-context flags — delivered as stage-named queries plus a findings memo with caveats. The window-program capstone: five cuts, one staged pipeline family, cited sentences.
requirements: Cut 1 — deterministic global leaderboard: ROW_NUMBER with unique tiebreaker over hours, full ordered list
Cut 2 — top-3 per role via partitioned ranking with outer filter; state the tie policy and its consequence
Cut 3 — NTILE(4) tiers with sizes verified (expect 4,4,3,3) and as-of dating on the labels
Cut 4 — cliff analysis: LAG gaps ordered DESC with the top-3 structural breaks named
Cut 5 — fusion: tier + role_avg + vs_role flags in one staged query; list every tier-vs-context mismatch explicitly
Memo: five finding bullets (tier composition, biggest cliff, mismatch learners, role comparison, data caveats), each citing its cut
technical: Flat grounding queries run in the SQL Query Sandbox; all window SQL runs in real SQLite or PostgreSQL
Every window query states its frame explicitly; every ranking states its tie policy
Tier sizes and cliff arithmetic hand-verified on at least two rows per cut
Engine-variant constructs (GROUPS/EXCLUDE) flagged with support notes, not assumed
project.architecture: Three sections: (1) Leaderboard suite — cuts 1–2 with tie policies and shortlists; (2) Tier & cliff analysis — cuts 3–5 with the fusion query and mismatch table; (3) Findings memo — five cited bullets plus caveats (n-sizes, tier drift, tie handling) and one proposal (which segment to intervene on first, backed by numbers).
steps: Ground in sandbox flats: range snapshot, role baselines, tie census — record all three tables
Build cuts in order (tiers → cliffs → fusion), verifying sizes and two hand-checked rows per cut
Write the memo last, once a mismatch or cliff has surprised you
Audit every query for explicit frames, deterministic orders, and outer filters
Flag engine-specific constructs; provide ROWS-based fallbacks where required
evaluation: Leaderboard deterministic (tiebreaker present); top-3 policy stated with consequence
Tier sizes verified 4,4,3,3 with as-of dating; cliffs ordered with top breaks named
Fusion flags every tier-vs-context mismatch; no bare partition averages presented as peer baselines
Memo bullets cite cuts and carry n-caveats; at least one non-obvious finding
All window SQL states frames; no QUALIFY-isms without emulation
stretch: Add moving-average trend (3-row) over hours with ROWS frame and interpret two inflections
Rebuild one cut with FILTER-based conditional metrics and compare readability
Benchmark the fusion query with EXPLAIN before/after an index and report

interviewQs.q: ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK — when each?
interviewQs.a: ROW_NUMBER (+ unique tiebreaker) for exact cardinalities: fixed feeds, pagination, dedup-by-first. RANK for honest shared placements with gaps: prizes, competitions. DENSE_RANK for tier labels without gaps. The through-line is tie contracts: arbitrary order, shared-with-skip, shared-dense — matched to product need (exact N vs honest ties vs tier names).

interviewQs.q: Why does LAST_VALUE need a frame when FIRST_VALUE seemingly doesn't?
interviewQs.a: FIRST_VALUE reads the partition/frame start, which the default growing frame always includes — correct by luck. LAST_VALUE reads the frame end, which under the default growing frame is the current row — 'last so far', almost never intended. The fix (ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) is mandatory pairing, and the asymmetry is the favorite window interview trap.

interviewQs.q: ROWS vs RANGE vs GROUPS — one-line each plus when it matters.
interviewQs.a: ROWS: physical positions — last-N readings, positional windows; ties split arbitrarily. RANGE: ORDER BY values — value bands where ties travel together; deterministic under ties. GROUPS: peer groups — tier-above/below logic without splitting tied tiers. It matters wherever ties exist: rankings, bands, and tier logic give different numbers per mode.

interviewQs.q: How do you filter on a window result in Postgres/SQLite, and why that shape?
interviewQs.a: Subquery/CTE wrapper: compute inside, filter outside — because windows evaluate after WHERE in the logical pipeline, so same-level filtering predates the alias. (Snowflake/BigQuery's QUALIFY is exactly this wrapper made syntax.) Same rule covers HAVING-like filtering on ranks and top-N-per-group patterns.

interviewQs.q: NTILE(4) = 1 shortlist: what do you tell stakeholders about stability?
interviewQs.a: Bucket sizes follow remainder rules (earlier buckets absorb extras) and boundaries drift as data grows — so persist labels with as-of dates, never compare undated tiers across runs, and pair shortlists with n-sizes. A top-quartile claim without dating and denominators is a future embarrassment.

interviewQs.q: Running total query returns per-row values that look like partial sums. Diagnosis?
interviewQs.a: Almost certainly correct behavior, not a bug: ORDER BY in OVER flips the default frame to growing-prefix (running semantics). If a grand total was intended, remove the ORDER BY or state the full-partition frame explicitly. The meta-lesson: defaults depend on ORDER BY presence, so always write frames explicitly — three words that delete the ambiguity.
